subject: AvalonBank: security & retention discussion — recap and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Chu <sylvia.chu@avalonbank.com>, TechOps <techops@avalonbank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: AvalonBank security & retention discussion — recap and proposed next steps

Sylvia / Peter / TechOps team — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap of what we covered on the call and the proposed path forward so everyone is aligned.

Key pain points we heard
- Long-term retention requirements: legal needs call for "7+ years" for transaction metadata and audit trails; you also need an approved deletion workflow for PII after retention windows expire.
- Audit logs & integrity: the security team requires tamper-evident audit logs and a sample retention export during procurement.
- SOC 2 attestation & pen test visibility: Avalon prefers vendors with a SOC 2 Type II report and recent pen test summary, plus an evidence manifest for the auditor.
- DPA & data flow clarity: procurement needs a DPA draft showing data residency, subprocessors, and deletion controls.

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- SOC 2 summary (attached) plus evidence manifest outlining where artifacts live and owner contacts.
- Audit-log export capability: immutable append-only logs, configurable retention windows, and sample exports in text/CSV (we included a small sample file).
- DPA template and standard subprocessors; we can mark the contract to add your required clauses for retention and deletion.
- Pen test process: we can share our latest summary and, under NDA, full test reports if needed.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
1) I’ll send a short evidence package by EOD tomorrow (SOC 2 summary + evidence_manifest.xlsx + audit-log sample). (Owner: Marissa) — target: 2026-06-23
2) Your security/techops to confirm whether a 7-year retention window (transaction metadata only) is acceptable, and specify any encryption/KMS requirements. (Owner: Avalon) — target: 2026-06-25
3) Technical deep-dive to validate export formats (syslog/CSV) and retention automation; schedule 60-minute session with Rishi and your TechOps. (Owner: Redwood + Avalon) — target: schedule by 2026-06-26
4) Procurement to review DPA + minimal contract redlines; we’ll prepare a tracked DPA with retention language. (Owner: Redwood + Avalon) — target: 2026-06-30

Attachments included: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, evidence_manifest.xlsx, redwood_audit-log-sample.txt

If this matches your expectations, please reply with any corrections and availability for the technical deep-dive (Rishi is available Tue/Wed mornings PT).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AvalonBank security & retention discussion — recap and proposed next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. A couple clarifying items from our side: 

1) Retention: the 7-year retention is for transaction metadata only (no full message content). We need confirmation that deletion is irreversible and auditable.
2) Audit logs: can you provide a sample export of a 90-day window (not production data) and a description of the tamper-evidence mechanism?
3) SOC 2: we require either full SOC 2 Type II or a SOC 2 + compensating control package. If you only provide a summary, we’ll need a path to the full report under NDA.
4) Pen test: high level findings are fine for initial review; our security lead may request the full report after procurement review.

Also: procurement specifically asked for the DPA to include a clause that specifies the retention period and an automated deletion certification every quarter. Please include that language in the draft DPA.

We’re tentatively OK to proceed to a tech call — Tue/Wed next week works for TechOps.

-Sylvia
Sylvia Chu
Head of Security Engineering, AvalonBank
sylvia.chu@avalonbank.com

Sylvia / team — attaching the items we discussed. Quick notes inline below.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (PDF, 220KB); evidence_manifest.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB); redwood_audit-log-sample.txt (TXT, 12KB)

redwood_soc2_summary.pdf — high-level table of covered controls, date range for last assessment, and auditor contact. If you want the full report we can share under NDA; we’ll start that process as soon as you confirm an NDA route.

evidence_manifest.xlsx — lists primary artifacts, their location (internal repo or Drive), retention owners, and an estimated time to produce during an audit. Notes column flags items that require privileged access.

redwood_audit-log-sample.txt — small, sanitized export of append-only audit log entries with timestamp, actor_id, resource, action, and a SHA256 hash column representing the log entry signature. This demonstrates the tamper-evidence approach: each entry is hashed and anchored to a chained HMAC — we can provide a short whitepaper for your auditors.

DPA language proposal (summary): 
- Retention clause will allow customer-configured retention windows down to the field level; we will include a 7-year default for transaction metadata if you require it.
- Automated deletion certification: we can provide an automated quarterly attestation that deletes past retention windows and a deletion-report artifact that includes SHA256 of deleted bundles for your records.

Next steps I can take immediately:
- Initiate NDA routing to share full SOC 2 and pen test report (if you confirm NDA contact).
- Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Rishi to validate export format and retention automation. I’ll share Rishi’s available slots.
- Drop a tracked DPA with the proposed retention and deletion certification clause into the HubSpot deal so procurement can comment.

If that works I’ll inbox a calendar invite for the tech call and ping procurement with the DPA draft.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Sylvia / TechOps team — looping in a quick note from the engineering side. Thanks for the level of detail; a couple of items we’ll plan to cover in the tech deep-dive:

- Export formats: we support syslog v.5424, gzipped CSV, and structured JSON lines; I’ll bring sample export scripts and a small data-dictionary for the transaction metadata fields.
- Tamper evidence: I’ll demo how the chained HMAC works and a simple verification script you can run on a sample export.
- Retention automation: show the retention policy UI (field-level rules) and the deletion certification artifact generation (SHA256 manifest + timestamp + signer).
- KMS & key rotation: confirm we can use customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) for encryption-at-rest and outline rotation cadence.

Suggested slots (PT):
- Tue 2026-06-29 09:00–10:00
- Wed 2026-06-30 10:00–11:00

If one of these works I’ll send an invite and attach a short agenda. Also: I placed the technical artifacts and sample scripts into a restricted Drive folder (link below). If you’d like the full SOC 2 or pen test reports we’ll need an NDA; Marissa will route that.
